title: Evidentiary Hearing (e.g., Following an Ex Parte Custody/Parenting-Time Order)
what_it_is: A hearing at which live testimony and exhibits are received under the Michigan Rules of Evidence, most commonly required after an ex parte order that could alter a child's established custodial environment (MCR 3.207(B)(1)(b)) or in any other matter the court sets for full proof.
who_is_in_the_room: You and the other party (or counsel).
sequence: An ex parte order is entered that could alter the child's established custodial environment; the court must schedule an evidentiary hearing within 21 days of entry, with notice included in the ex parte order (MCR 3.207(B)(1)(b)).
Discovery/subpoenas are arranged in advance (unrepresented parties must move the court for a non-party discovery subpoena; the clerk can issue a hearing subpoena - MCR 2.305(A)(1); MCR 2.506(B)(1)).
The hearing is held on the record; testimony is live except by telephone for good cause or under MCR 2.407 (MCR 3.210(A)(4)).
Findings are entered; on a contested postjudgment motion to modify, findings of fact and conclusions of law are required (MCR 3.210(D)(1)).
prepare: A proof table: for each element the court must find, the exhibit and the sponsoring witness.
Foundation scripts for each exhibit type (text thread, screenshot, photo, recording, records) - see L1 guide.
A clear statement of whether you concede the child's established custodial environment - conceding what is true is not a loss (Vodvarka/ Pierron doctrine).

applicable_rules.summary: The court must not issue an order that could alter a child's established custodial environment without also scheduling an evidentiary hearing under MCL 722.27, to be held within 21 days after entry.
Testimony must be taken in person except by telephone for good cause or by videoconference under MCR 2.407/2.408.
Findings of fact and conclusions of law are required on contested postjudgment motions to modify a final judgment or order.

deadlines.label: Evidentiary hearing held after an ex parte custody/parenting-time order
Motion to amend/add findings after entry

traps.safe_move: Michigan has no self-authentication route for digital records (MRE 902 ends at (11)). Every digital exhibit needs a sponsoring witness.

traps.trap: Building any part of the case on what the child said.
traps.safe_move: MRE 803A's child-hearsay exception is criminal/delinquency-proceedings only. Do not rely on it here.
Ask for findings on the record on contested points; without them there is nothing to object to later.

traps.trap: Offering your own letters for their truth.
traps.safe_move: Offer them only to show the request was made and its date (MRE 801(c)(2)) - state the limited purpose out loud; PROVISIONAL, no case read applying this framing.

do_not: Never characterize the other parent with a clinical label as a pleaded claim (narcissist, alienator, PAS, coercive control) - GUARDRAILS.md S2.
Never use the child as a witness, messenger, interviewee, or source, and never record the child - GUARDRAILS.md S8, absolute.
Never assert that any recording you made is lawful - Michigan law is unsettled and the exposure is criminal.
Never sign or stipulate to anything on the spot without reading it fully first.

openers: Good morning/afternoon, Your Honor. My name is [Party], and I am representing myself.
I am here to address [narrow issue]. I have [N] exhibits and a short chronology.
closers: I don't have that information, but I can provide records if needed.
I'd like the record to reflect [narrow, factual point] and I reserve my right to address anything broader in the appropriate forum.

safety_gates: immediate danger -> 911, do not proceed on this guide alone
PPO/DV/CPS contact live -> stop, safety resources, do not proceed on this guide alone
UCCJEA/interstate fact -> stop, MC 416 affidavit guidance
recording question in any form -> unsettled law, criminal exposure, attorney question only
child asked/expected to speak to anyone about the case -> stop
exit_checklist: Write down the date, who appeared, and what was decided or taken under advisement before leaving the building.
Write on any document handed to you the date you received it - that date can start a clock.
Calendar every deadline this event started, counted from the earliest possible trigger date.
Note whether anything was requested that you did not have time to answer fully, and follow up in writing.
